before.root_cause: interleaved calibrated the same cand_run callable independently under candidate and candidate_copy_control; after warm-up it selected k=10 and k=17. Different fixed command-buffer overhead per iteration created a systematic wall-clock A/A bias.

fix.rule: calibrate each callable object once and reuse the same k for every alias; distinct runners keep independent calibration
unchanged: shared runner, candidate bytes, execution geometry and launch path
GPU timestamp statistic used by tcenv ab
reports without --control have no second arm and take the old path

after_first_run_calibration.note: An external sitecustomize logger recorded one choose_iters call for the shared candidate/control callable. The independent ab arms intentionally have different runners and their own k values.

conclusion: The reproduced calibration bias is fixed on this fixture: all three shared-control intervals contain 1.0 and all probe checks pass. The control remains wall-clock while ab remains GPU-timestamp; their absolute medians must not be conflated. resolvable_relative is a measured property of each window, not a universal 0.5% guarantee.
